key_result: Measured title-free SQLite page+all-revision occurrence schema fits projected4GB aggregate for realistic and ID-onlyint64 scenarios. SQLite is not ruled out; custom packing is not required by measured capacity alone.

projection_basis.each_component: SQLite dbstat per-table and group-offset-index bytes scaled independently to exact25,792,234pages/257,960groups/30Mrevisioncap; not whole-DB/page ratio ignoringrevisioncap.

why_no_duplicate_page_ID_map: Existing immutable globally-unique index remains the source pageID→ordinal/title/group map. A future native producer must match EVERY native occurrence to the same indexed page ordinal/ID/title/group and exact25,792,234coverage. Only that full ordered reconciliation transfers uniqueness to native pages. Current measurements do not claim that native reconciliation happened.
revision_custody: WITHOUT ROWID primary key(revision_id,page_ordinal,revision_ordinal) indexes nonunique revision-ID lookup and retains cross-page and same-page repeated IDs as separate occurrences; no canonical selection/dedup/overwrite. Page rawgroup-local span+SHA references original complete native XML; revisionordinal allows later recovery without copying all native text.
special_cases: Redirect/deleted-text flags, nonzero namespaces, unknown model enum needing future exception context, three100MB metadata-only oversize records perfixture,1.16rev/page mixed case, IDs-only8byte stress, and separately extreme all-fields int64 stress. No large text bodies allocated.
extreme_case_scope: All-fields int64 stress projects3.846GBDB and4.038GBincludingreserves and therefore fails both caps. It is not a plausible population model under256GBtotaldecodedXML: all25Mpagescannot each have2**48textbytes/2**51rawbytes. It demonstrates a finite schema/cap limit, not proof of actual infeasibility. IDs-only int64 stress still fits with10%DBmargin. Actual unknown scalar distributions and fragmentation can still exhaust the cap and must stopPARTIAL.

packed_comparison.differences: Packed proposal includes namespace ordinal vector and external sort temporary runs plus extra revision-span sidecar. SQLite instead uses SQL filters/scans fornamespace/flags, reuses existing index forpageIDlookup, and composite revision Btree with page span+revisionordinal forsource recovery. No on-disk sort/journal overlap in MEMORY mode; power/forced-kill partialDB not promisedrecoverable.

performance_limits: 500kcase wholeDB exceeds32MiBcache, but its revisionBtree is only~9.8MB and fitscache; full30M random-indexI/O is not benchmarked.
Synthetic insert throughput excludes native XML tokenization/hash/semanticidentity checks and full-size DB integrity/publication costs. No forecast or total nativeproducer runtime certified.
Small ordered/permuted results differ in Btreefill; no globalSQLite size guarantee from linear extrapolation.
Existing packed time estimates derive from a biased1600pageprefix, not a measured fullproducer. This assessment does not validate them.
